steps.title: Rich dishes
steps.body: Marsanne's body and texture suit rich dishes: roast chicken, veal in cream sauce, lobster, crab, scallops, and dishes with butter or almonds. Aged white Hermitage suits truffle, mushrooms and hard cheeses like Comté. Avoid very acidic or very spicy food.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 11 to 13 degrees, not too cold. Simple Marsanne is good young. White Hermitage is best either within two to three years or after ten. Tahbilk's aged Marsanne shows how unoaked versions develop too.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits an aged white Hermitage?
steps.explanation: Rich, earthy dishes match its honeyed, nutty development.

steps.body: Decant an older white Hermitage. Like a red, it benefits from air, opening its nutty, honeyed aromas.

steps.explanation: Acidic dressings make low-acid wines taste flat.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Marsanne suits lobster, veal and Comté
Drink white Hermitage young or after ten years
